title: BPI Ri 1 (BPI Ri1) Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: BPI Ri 1 Rice Variety: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: BPI Ri 1 is a glutinous inbred rice for irrigated lowland: about 120 days and 4.3 tonnes per hectare on average. See its pest ratings and grain quality.
excerpt: BPI Ri 1 is a glutinous inbred rice variety for irrigated lowland, known locally as BPI Ri1. PhilRice lists it from 1979. BPI bred it. It matures in about 120 days and averages 4.3 tonnes per hectare.

heroImage.alt: An irrigated palay field in the Philippines, where BPI Ri 1 is meant to grow

blocks.text: If you came here looking for rice variety 1, or Rc 1, this is the one. The facts below come from sources that include PhilRice and its public seed database. So you can compare it with the other varieties in our [rice variety finder](/rice-varieties) before you buy seed. Also read our guide to [rice varieties in the Philippines](/crops/rice-varieties-philippines) for how inbreds, hybrids and special rice differ.

items: **Yield:** 4.3 tonnes per hectare on average, or about 86 cavans of 50 kilograms.
**Holds up against:** rice blast, bacterial leaf blight, tungro.

blocks.text: How much does BPI Ri 1 yield?

On average it gives 4.3 tonnes per hectare. That is about 86 cavans of 50 kilograms of palay. It sits below the average of the 118 irrigated lowland inbreds in PhilRice's list, which is 5.2 tonnes. So plan your costs on the average, then work toward the top with the habits in our guide to [raising rice yield per hectare](/blog/increase-rice-yield-per-hectare).
How many days does it take to mature?

It takes about 120 days from sowing to harvest. IRRI groups varieties of 100 to 120 days as short duration and 120 to 140 days as medium, so this one counts as short duration. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains turn golden yellow, as PalayCheck advises. Because the day count drives every task, anee.io counts it for you from each lot's own planting day, with the [growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in PhilRice's tests: R resistant, MR moderately resistant, I intermediate, MS moderately susceptible, S susceptible. Some carry a second rating in brackets, as PhilRice lists them.

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings PhilRice lists. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain of a disease or a new pest population comes. So keep scouting, and use our [pest and disease finders](/features/pest-and-disease-finders) when something looks wrong.

It suits irrigated lowland, where you control the water. Level the field well so the water stands evenly, and plant at the same time as your neighbors, one of the PalayCheck key checks, so pests cannot move from field to field. Our guide to [rice land preparation](/land-preparation/rice-land-preparation) shows each step. PhilRice recommends it for the dry season and the wet season. You can plant it dry direct seeded, transplanted or wet direct seeded. For the right month in your province, see [the best time to plant rice](/blog/best-time-to-plant-rice-philippines).

items.q: What is the local name of BPI Ri 1?
items.a: It is known as BPI Ri1. Seed sellers and agriculturists use both names, so ask for either one.

items.q: How many days does BPI Ri 1 take to harvest?
items.a: About 120 days after sowing. Then harvest when 85 to 90 percent of the grains are golden yellow.

items.q: What is the average yield of BPI Ri 1?
items.a: PhilRice lists 4.3 tonnes per hectare on average, about 86 cavans of 50 kilograms. Your own yield depends on water, seed, fertilizer and timing.

items.q: In which season should I plant it?
items.a: PhilRice recommends it for the dry season and the wet season. Then pick the month with our planting calendar guide and the forecast for your town.
No, it is an inbred. So the seed you buy grows true, but certified seed still gives the best start, as PalayCheck advises.

items.q: Where can I buy certified seed of this variety?
items.a: Ask accredited seed growers in your province, your municipal agriculturist or the nearest PhilRice station. Look for the certified seed tag on the sack before you pay.
